title: Accounts Administrator
description:
Transaction Recruitment are supporting a well-established professional services business based in Leamington, in their search for an Accounts Administrator to join them on a permanent basis. Reporting to the Head of Accounts, you'll help keep the department running smoothly, handling the daily flow of money in and out of the business with accuracy and care.

This is a varied, hands-on role that combines banking, ledger work and reconciliations with regular contact with colleagues, clients and external parties. You'll be trusted with confidential information and client funds, so a careful, compliance-minded approach is essential. This position is fully office based.

Key Responsibilities:
- Checking bank receipts daily, logging them, and updating systems when funds are received and posted
- Preparing paying-in books and processing cheque, CHAPS and BACS payments, including checking and authorising payments entered by colleagues
- Confirming sufficient cleared funds are held on client ledgers before any payment is made
- Posting payments, journals and client invoices accurately, and transferring funds between client, office and deposit accounts in line with SRA Accounts Rules and in-house policies
- Reconciling bank accounts daily and completing month-end reconciliations, including the consolidated client account reconciliation
- Allocating expenses to the correct nominal codes and cost centres
- Inputting supplier invoices to the purchase ledger, paying them when due, and resolving queries with suppliers
- Processing card payments and managing the petty cash, including weekly reconciliation
- Handling department calls and enquiries from clients, banks and auditors, and keeping filing and documentation in order for audit

In return my client offers a working environment which promotes work/life balance, free on-site parking and easy access by public transport. They are proud of their low turnover in staff and are looking for their newest team member quickly.

title: Accounts Payable
description:
Senior Accounts Payable Specialist - 12-Month Fixed-Term Contract
Location: Coventry
Working Pattern: Hybrid - 3 days per week in the office
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced and detail-focused Senior Accounts Payable Specialist to join our Finance team in Coventry on a 12-month fixed-term contract, covering maternity leave.

This is a hands-on role with responsibility for the end-to-end Accounts Payable process across multiple international entities. You will play a key role in ensuring invoices, payments, expenses and reconciliations are processed accurately, efficiently and in line with company policies and regulatory requirements.

The role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with 3 days per week based in our Coventry office.

The role would suit an experienced Accounts Payable professional who is confident working independently, enjoys solving problems and is comfortable taking ownership of processes while working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
Accounts Payable
Manage the end-to-end Accounts Payable process, from invoice receipt through to processing and payment.
Review and process invoices accurately, including multi-currency invoices across multiple entities.
Manage invoices requiring additional information or approval, following up with relevant stakeholders to ensure timely resolution.
Ensure invoices are correctly coded, allocated and recorded.
Process direct debit transactions and ensure accurate allocation and reconciliation.
Maintain accurate supplier accounts and resolve discrepancies promptly.
Complete supplier statement reconciliations and investigate outstanding items.
Review debit balances and overpayments, taking appropriate action to resolve discrepancies.
Support the timely completion of payment runs, ensuring agreed payment terms are maintained.

Expenses & Corporate Cards
Take ownership of the corporate card process, ensuring information is received promptly and transactions are processed and reconciled accurately.
Manage employee expenses across multiple international locations, ensuring compliance with company policy and relevant VAT and tax requirements.
Monitor expense reporting and identify recurring issues or areas requiring further guidance.
Support the wider business with guidance and education around expenses and policy compliance.

Systems, Data & Controls
Maintain accurate Accounts Payable master data and ensure appropriate controls are maintained.
Monitor supplier records and minimise duplicate accounts.
Work effectively with finance and workflow systems to manage transactions, approvals, queries and reporting.
Support the maintenance and development of invoice processing and automation processes.
Identify opportunities to improve Accounts Payable processes, controls and efficiency.

Month-End
Complete all Accounts Payable month-end activities within agreed deadlines.
Perform relevant reconciliations and ensure the Accounts Payable ledger is accurate.
Investigate and correct discrepancies promptly.
Ensure Accounts Payable balances reconcile appropriately to the wider financial records.
Escalate any unresolved issues to the AP Manager in a timely manner.
Produce and maintain accurate reports to support month-end and wider Finance requirements.
Team Support
Work collaboratively within the Finance team while demonstrating the ability to work independently.
Build strong working relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
Support the AP Manager with ad-hoc duties and projects as required.
Provide support and oversight to the AP team when the AP Manager is absent.
Assist with business training and guidance relating to Accounts Payable and expenses processes.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across the Finance function.

About You
You will ideally have:

3-5+ years' experience in Accounts Payable, ideally within a multi-entity or international environment.
Strong knowledge of Accounts Payable processes, controls and best practice.
Experience with invoice processing, supplier reconciliations, payment runs and month-end activities.
Experience working with multiple currencies and international entities is desirable.
Good understanding of expenses, VAT and relevant regulatory requirements.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach.
Strong Excel and Microsoft Office skills.
Experience using an ERP or finance system.
Previous experience providing support or supervision to colleagues would be advantageous.

Key Attributes
Highly organised with excellent time-management skills.
Comfortable working to tight deadlines and managing competing priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Confident dealing with internal and external stakeholders.
Able to build effective relationships with suppliers and colleagues.
Proactive, reliable and able to use initiative.
Strong team player who is equally comfortable working independently.
Committed to accuracy, process improvement and delivering a high standard of work.

title: Payroll Administrator
company: Trinity House Group Ltd - Agency - Contract
description:
Payroll Administrator
This is a chance to get hands-on with one of the biggest payroll changes in years. From April 2027, benefits in kind have to be processed through payroll, and you will be right at the heart of making that happen, from the very first workshops through to go-live. It is a 6 month contract with a clear goal, and the kind of project experience payroll teams everywhere are going to be looking for.
This would suit a Payroll Administrator who knows SAP and has been involved in a payroll project or system change before. You will be the person who keeps on top of the detail: what has been agreed, what has been tested and what still needs fixing. If you are available now and like the idea of seeing a project through from start to finish, this one is for you.

What You Will Be Doing
- Working as dedicated support to the Payroll Manager leading the benefits in kind implementation, helping keep the project on track for April 2027
- Getting involved in requirements gathering workshops and stakeholder meetings from day one
- Documenting business requirements, actions, decisions and process changes so everyone is clear on what has been agreed
- Validating payroll data in SAP, completing reconciliations and pulling together analysis ahead of go-live
- Preparing for and running system integration testing, parallel runs and user acceptance testing
- Logging testing defects and chasing each one through to resolution
- Checking payroll calculations and outputs to make sure benefits are flowing through correctly
- Producing project reporting and governance documentation
- Supporting training, communications and business readiness so people know exactly what is changing
- Working alongside a wider change programme, with a new HR system and a new time and attendance system going in at the same time, and helping hand everything over smoothly into business as usual

What We Need From You
- SAP payroll experience is essential. You have worked in SAP and are comfortable finding your way around it
- A solid payroll administration background. You understand how a payroll actually runs, start to finish
- A good understanding of UK payroll legislation. CIPP qualified or working towards it would be a real bonus
- Some experience of a payroll project or system change, whether that is testing, a parallel run or a migration
- Strong Excel skills, as you will be validating and reconciling a lot of data
- Someone who genuinely cares about getting it right. You will be checking calculations before they go live, so accuracy really matters here
- A confident communicator who is happy speaking up in workshops and can juggle competing priorities without losing track
- Available immediately or on a short notice period, as they are keen to get someone started straight away

What's in it for you
- Proper flexibility, with just 1-2 days a week in the office and the rest working from home
- A genuinely exciting project to get stuck into, with a new payroll setup, a new HR system and a new time and attendance system all landing at once
- Benefits in kind payrolling on your CV before the April 2027 deadline, which is exactly the experience every payroll team is about to be hunting for
- The full project journey, from the first workshop right through testing to go-live, so you get to see your hard work really pay off
- £(phone number removed)k depending on experience, for 37.5 hours a week
- A quick, painless process with a single stage Teams interview, so you could be starting straight away

If this sounds like the project for you and you have the SAP payroll experience to back it up, we would love to hear from you, so apply today.

title: Payroll Officer
company: ROSE & YOUNG RECRUITMENT LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
Part-Time Payroll Officer/Specialist - CPP Qualified

Location: Coventry

Employment Type: Part-time hours considered - 3 days per week on site

Salary: £30,000 - £32,000 per annum pro-rated

Department: Finance / Payroll

Reports to: Head of HR

About the Role

Our client is seeking an experienced Payroll Specialist with CPP (Certified Payroll Professional) qualification and a strong background in the education sector to join their finance team.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the accurate and timely administration of payroll, ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, policies, and internal procedures. You will bring strong technical payroll knowledge together with an understanding of the complexities of payroll within an educational environment, including academic staff, support staff, variable contracts, benefits, deductions, and multiple pay arrangements.

This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organised payroll professional who takes pride in accuracy, confidentiality, and delivering a high-quality service to employees and management.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage the end-to-end payroll process accurately and efficiently.
- Process monthly/biweekly payroll for teaching, administrative, and support staff.
- Review and validate payroll data, including new starters, leavers, salary changes, promotions, deductions, and contractual amendments.
- Ensure payroll calculations are accurate and completed within established deadlines.
- Administer pensions, benefits, statutory deductions, garnishments, and other payroll-related adjustments.
- Maintain accurate and confidential employee payroll records.
- Reconcile payroll reports and investigate and resolve discrepancies.
- Prepare payroll reports and provide relevant information to Finance and senior management.
- Ensure compliance with payroll legislation, tax requirements, pension regulations, and organisational policies.
- Respond professionally and promptly to employee payroll queries.
- Work closely with HR and Finance to ensure employee records and payroll information are accurate and up to date.
- Support internal and external payroll audits.
- Maintain appropriate payroll documentation and ensure strong controls are followed.
- Identify opportunities to improve payroll processes, systems, and reporting.
- Maintain strict confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and financial information.

Experience within an educational organisation is highly desirable. The successful candidate will ideally understand the payroll requirements associated with schools, colleges, universities, academies, or other education-focused organisations.

Experience working with a diverse workforce, including teaching staff, academic professionals, administrators, and support personnel, would be particularly valuable.

Essential Qualifications & Experience
- CPP (Certified Payroll Professional) qualification.
- Proven experience working in payroll, ideally managing payroll from start to finish.
- Preference to those with experience within the education sector.
- Strong understanding of payroll legislation, taxation, pensions, and statutory requirements.
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent organisational and time-management abilities.
- Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Proficiency with payroll and HR systems and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with HR, Finance, and other departments.
- Experience supporting payroll audits and compliance reviews.
- Experience improving payroll processes or implementing payroll systems.

title: Purchase Ledger Administrator
description:

Salary: £21,200 £22,400 per annum (30 hours per week, equivalent to £26,500 £28,000 full-time), plus up to 10% bonus and hybrid working.

We are currently recruiting for a Purchase Ledger Administrator to join our team in Stratford-upon-Avon. This is a part-time, hybrid role working 30 hours per week, offering a flexible blend of office and home-based working.

As a Purchase Ledger Administrator, you ll be the key point of contact for all internal and external queries related to Accounts Payable. Working closely with the wider finance team, you ll ensure the smooth and accurate processing of purchase invoices, staff expenses, and supplier payments.
